narrative.overview: The app is a writer's desk at night. The page is paper under a desk lamp; the work happens on a sheet laid over it, with a second sheet peeking out underneath. Navigation is folder tabs; optional tools sit in a desk rail. The feel is tactile and playful inside a calm, readable frame: buttons press, cards settle with a small overshoot, the spin wheel lands, ticks and posts arrive in order. Type and the turn colours carry the personality, not decoration. Dark mode is a re-tinted night desk.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, one sheet per page, a second sheet behind it.
Young Serif headlines, Figtree interface text, Newsreader for writing and premises.
Turn colours as the product's own language: plum for your turn, blue outline for their turn, a quiet brown for queued.
One filled sage button per area; everything else secondary or text.
Springy, physical motion that switches off completely under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Turn Colour Rule
rules.body: Plum, blue and brown mean your turn, their turn and queued. Never use them as decoration or for anything else.

rules.name: The One Sage Button Rule
rules.body: Each region gets at most one filled sage button. Everything else is secondary, text or danger.

rules.name: The Tinted Text Rule
rules.body: Labels on tinted surfaces use soft ink, not faint ink, so they pass AA in both themes.

rules.name: The 12px Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing people read is set below 12px.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No small label sits above a heading. The heading carries its own weight; type information goes after the title, not above it.

rules.name: The One Elevation Rule
rules.body: A surface declares elevation once: a hairline or a shadow, never both.

rules.name: The No Nested Cards Rule
rules.body: A card never sits inside another card. Group inner items with a tint or a hairline instead.

dos: Do keep the Writer's Desk tokens; desk themes may change only the accent and its tint.
Do use one filled sage button per region.
Do keep turn colours for turn meaning only: plum yours, blue outline theirs, brown queued.
Do set the writer's words in Newsreader and interface text in Figtree.
Do run motion on the --motion-* and --ease-* tokens so reduced motion turns it off.
Do keep touch targets at 44px on phones and text at 12px or larger.
donts: Don't put a small label above a heading.
Don't nest cards, or give one surface both a hairline and a shadow.
Don't add a bar down one side of a rounded box.
Don't hard-code colours in components; only canvas export and trading-card themes hold colours as data.
Don't use faint ink on tinted surfaces.
